findings.issue_text: `.small-action-desc` loses the 4em left padding that cleared the inline topic-avatar, so the description text and sibling buttons will visually collide with or butt against the avatar in the new flex layout (topic-post.scss ~277-280)

`.small-action` flex container with default `flex-wrap: nowrap` changes vertical stacking to a single row; multiple children (avatar + desc + action button) will be squeezed horizontally, and old-2009-syntax browsers have no wrap mode at all (topic-post.scss ~261-263)

Invalid `-ms-align-items` property in the align-items mixin (mixins.scss ~line 121); IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align` which is already emitted, so it's dead code that creates a misleading divergence risk if edited

`order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` is a no-op because it's nested inside `.title` (not a direct flex child of `.contents`), and `.panel`'s `order(3)` matches DOM order only by luck; future DOM changes can silently break visual vs. keyboard/screen-reader order, with inconsistent `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` behavior in old WebKits (topic.scss ~29-30, header.scss ~36-39)

Removing `.title { float: left }` leaves the title as a flex item with default `flex-shrink: 1` and no min-width constraint, so long header titles can shrink/wrap/clip on narrow viewports, especially under old-2009 flexbox where items shrink proportionally (header.scss ~16-20)
Invalid vendor property `-ms-align-items` emitted in the align-items mixin in mixins.scss; correct IE10 syntax is `-ms-flex-align`, indicating the prefixed value mapping is unverified

IE10 will fail to parse `baseline` in `-ms-flex-align: baseline` (used in badges.css.scss) since the real `-ms-flex-align` uses center/flex-start/flex-end/stretch values, falling back to default alignment and causing minor IE10 visual inconsistency
The align-items mixin in mixins.scss:~117 emits -ms-align-items, a non-existent property in any browser engine (correct IE10 syntax is -ms-flex-align), producing dead CSS shipped on every page load

Legacy 2009/2012-spec flexbox prefixes in mixins.scss:99-130 emit 4-5 declarations where one suffices, tripling output size of every flex usage and compounding bloat as mixins are reused across the codebase

The old 2009 -webkit-box/-moz-box flexbox model has different semantics (box-align ≠ align-items for some values, box-ordinal-group packing rules), so layouts can silently differ in old engines and cause relayouts/extra reflows
order() usages (.panel { @include order(3); }, .extra-info-wrapper { @include order(2); }) may tie with explicit order: 1 elements in old-spec engines and fall back to DOM order, shifting paint order
margin-left: auto on .panel is a no-op in the 2009 box model, potentially reintroducing the collapsed layout and causing layout thrash on resize

RTL breakage: replacing float: right with margin-left: auto in header.scss .panel is not direction-safe — margin-left: auto is not flipped by RTL processing, so the panel sits on the wrong side in RTL locales

Visual order ≠ DOM/focus order: flex order on .panel and .extra-info-wrapper changes paint order but not tab/screen-reader order, causing keyboard focus mismatch on header controls and unintended layout changes for other order-0 children
-ms-align-items in mixins.scss is a nonexistent property (the real IE10 property is -ms-flex-align), making it a silent no-op that misleads readers into thinking legacy support exists

Mixing 2009 (display: -webkit-box / -webkit-box-ordinal-group) and 2012 flexbox syntaxes in mixins.scss produces inconsistent fallback layouts on legacy browsers, with -moz-box-ordinal-group unsupported in Firefox web content
.small-action flex layout in topic-post.scss removes the 4em avatar clearance so .small-action-desc text touches the avatar edge, and changes spacing of avatar-less small-action blocks
Flex shrink on header.scss .contents allows a long title/category badge to compress the panel buttons (hamburger, search, user) at narrow desktop widths since no flex-shrink: 0 or min-width is set

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `.small-action-desc` loses the 4em left padding that cleared the inline topic-avatar, so the description text and sibling buttons will visually collide with or butt against the avatar in the new flex layout (topic-post.scss ~277-280)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `.small-action` to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) and removes the old float/clear-style spacing approach by changing `.small-action-desc` padding from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`. In a flex layout, the `.topic-avatar` and `.small-action-desc` are laid out as separate flex items, so the description text should not overlap the avatar in the way the finding implies; the removed 4em padding was primarily needed for non-flex/float layouts. The diff alone doesn’t verify an actual collision/overlap defect (at most, spacing may be tighter).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `.small-action` flex container with default `flex-wrap: nowrap` changes vertical stacking to a single row; multiple children (avatar + desc + action button) will be squeezed horizontally, and old-2009-syntax browsers have no wrap mode at all (topic-post.scss ~261-263)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `.small-action` to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) without setting `flex-wrap`, so it will default to `nowrap` and lay out its children (e.g., `.topic-avatar`, `.small-action-desc`, and any other siblings) in a single row. This is a real layout-behavior change compared to the previous block layout, and could cause horizontal squeezing/overflow on narrow widths unless other rules constrain it. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove it will break in practice (it may be intended), so it’s more of a potential/edge-case layout concern than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Invalid `-ms-align-items` property in the align-items mixin (mixins.scss ~line 121); IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align` which is already emitted, so it's dead code that creates a misleading divergence risk if edited

`order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` is a no-op because it's nested inside `.title` (not a direct flex child of `.contents`), and `.panel`'s `order(3)` matches DOM order only by luck; future DOM changes can silently break visual vs. keyboard/screen-reader order, with inconsistent `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` behavior in old WebKits (topic.scss ~29-30, header.scss ~36-39)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `@include order(2)` added to `.extra-info-wrapper` (topic.scss) and `@include order(3)` added to `.panel` (header.scss), but it does not show the relevant HTML/DOM nesting or which elements are direct children of the new flex container (`.contents` now includes `@include flexbox()`). Without markup, we cannot verify that `.extra-info-wrapper` is nested inside `.title` (and thus not a flex item) or that `.panel`’s ordering “matches DOM order only by luck.” The claims about keyboard/screen-reader order and old WebKit `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` behavior are also not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing `.title { float: left }` leaves the title as a flex item with default `flex-shrink: 1` and no min-width constraint, so long header titles can shrink/wrap/clip on narrow viewports, especially under old-2009 flexbox where items shrink proportionally (header.scss ~16-20)

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `.title { float: left; }` by moving flex layout onto `.contents` (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) and adjusts `.panel` with `margin-left: auto`/`order(3)`. However, the finding’s claim that the title will shrink due to default `flex-shrink: 1` and “no min-width constraint” isn’t supported by anything in the diff: there are no new `flex`/`flex-shrink`/`min-width`/overflow/wrapping rules shown for the title element, and the assertion about flex defaults/min-width behavior is not verifiable from this change alone. This is speculative and partially misstates flex item defaults rather than a concrete, diff-demonstrable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Invalid vendor property `-ms-align-items` emitted in the align-items mixin in mixins.scss; correct IE10 syntax is `-ms-flex-align`, indicating the prefixed value mapping is unverified

IE10 will fail to parse `baseline` in `-ms-flex-align: baseline` (used in badges.css.scss) since the real `-ms-flex-align` uses center/flex-start/flex-end/stretch values, falling back to default alignment and causing minor IE10 visual inconsistency

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `align-items($alignment)` mixin that emits `-ms-flex-align: $alignment`, and `badges.css.scss` calls it with `baseline`. However, the finding’s claim that IE10’s `-ms-flex-align` only accepts `center/flex-start/flex-end/stretch` misstates the old IE10 prefixed syntax (it doesn’t use `flex-start`/`flex-end` and `baseline` is not shown in the diff as inherently invalid). From the diff alone, you can’t verify an IE10 parse failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The align-items mixin in mixins.scss:~117 emits -ms-align-items, a non-existent property in any browser engine (correct IE10 syntax is -ms-flex-align), producing dead CSS shipped on every page load
matched_golden_ids: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue explicitly notes that the mixin emits -ms-align-items, which does not exist in IE/Edge, and identifies -ms-flex-align as the correct legacy property. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy 2009/2012-spec flexbox prefixes in mixins.scss:99-130 emit 4-5 declarations where one suffices, tripling output size of every flex usage and compounding bloat as mixins are reused across the codebase

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new flexbox-related mixins in mixins.scss (@mixin flexbox, inline-flex, align-items, order) that emit multiple vendor-prefixed declarations (e.g., -webkit-box/-moz-box/-ms-flexbox/-webkit-flex/flex). These are then used in several stylesheets, so the repeated multi-declaration output can increase compiled CSS size. This is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/performance concern rather than a functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The old 2009 -webkit-box/-moz-box flexbox model has different semantics (box-align ≠ align-items for some values, box-ordinal-group packing rules), so layouts can silently differ in old engines and cause relayouts/extra reflows

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds legacy 2009 flexbox syntax alongside modern flexbox via new mixins (e.g., `@mixin flexbox()` sets `display: -webkit-box; display: -moz-box; ... display: flex;`, and `@mixin align-items` sets `-webkit-box-align` as well as `align-items`). It also maps `order($val)` to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val`, which has different semantics (notably 1-based grouping vs modern `order`). This can cause different layouts in older engines that only support `-webkit-box/-moz-box`, but whether that’s a “defect” depends on supported browsers; the claimed reflow/relayout impact is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: order() usages (.panel { @include order(3); }, .extra-info-wrapper { @include order(2); }) may tie with explicit order: 1 elements in old-spec engines and fall back to DOM order, shifting paint order

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an `@mixin order($val)` that sets legacy `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group` to the same numeric `$val` as modern `order`. In the old 2009 flexbox spec, `box-ordinal-group` is effectively 1-based (default 1 corresponds to modern `order: 0`), so it typically needs an offset (+1) to match modern ordering. With new usages like `.panel { @include order(3); }` and `.extra-info-wrapper { @include order(2); }`, old-spec engines could compute a different visual order than modern engines, causing layout/paint order shifts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: margin-left: auto on .panel is a no-op in the 2009 box model, potentially reintroducing the collapsed layout and causing layout thrash on resize

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `.header .contents` from floats to flex (`@include flexbox()`) and then relies on `.panel { margin-left: auto; }` to push the panel to the right. The new `flexbox()` mixin includes legacy 2009 `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` declarations, where `margin-left: auto` is not a reliable way to create the “push to end” behavior (old box model typically uses `-webkit-box-pack`). This is a compatibility/layout concern grounded in the added mixins and the new `margin-left: auto`, but the specific claims about “collapsed layout” and “layout thrash on resize” are not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RTL breakage: replacing float: right with margin-left: auto in header.scss .panel is not direction-safe — margin-left: auto is not flipped by RTL processing, so the panel sits on the wrong side in RTL locales

adjudication.rationale: In header.scss, `.panel` changes from `float: right;` to `margin-left: auto;` inside a new flex container (`.contents { @include flexbox(); ... }`). `margin-left: auto` is a physical-side rule that pushes the item to the end only in LTR; in RTL it typically won’t place the item on the intended “right” side (you’d need `margin-right: auto` or logical margins). This can introduce incorrect header panel positioning in RTL layouts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Visual order ≠ DOM/focus order: flex order on .panel and .extra-info-wrapper changes paint order but not tab/screen-reader order, causing keyboard focus mismatch on header controls and unintended layout changes for other order-0 children

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces flexbox reordering via `@include order(3)` on `.panel` (header.scss) and `@include order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` (topic.scss). In flexbox, `order` changes the visual/paint order without changing DOM order, so keyboard tabbing and some assistive-tech reading order can remain in DOM order, potentially causing a focus/order mismatch. The claim about affecting other `order: 0` siblings is also a plausible consequence of adding `order` to one child within a flex container. The exact user-visible impact can’t be fully verified from the diff alone because the surrounding HTML/other flex children aren’t shown, but the diff-grounded concern is real and actionable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: -ms-align-items in mixins.scss is a nonexistent property (the real IE10 property is -ms-flex-align), making it a silent no-op that misleads readers into thinking legacy support exists

adjudication.rationale: In mixins.scss, the new `@mixin align-items($alignment)` includes both `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;` and `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. The latter is not a standard/known IE10 flexbox property and will be a no-op, which can mislead readers into thinking it provides legacy support. This doesn’t create a clear behavioral break because the correct `-ms-flex-align` is also present, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded issue worth fixing/clarifying.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mixing 2009 (display: -webkit-box / -webkit-box-ordinal-group) and 2012 flexbox syntaxes in mixins.scss produces inconsistent fallback layouts on legacy browsers, with -moz-box-ordinal-group unsupported in Firefox web content

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds flexbox mixins that combine multiple generations of syntax (e.g., `display: -webkit-box`/`-moz-box` alongside `display: -ms-flexbox`, `-webkit-flex`, `flex`, and `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` alongside `order`). While this is often intentional for compatibility, it can lead to differing behavior across legacy implementations (e.g., old box model vs modern flexbox ordering/alignment semantics). The specific claim about Firefox support for `-moz-box-ordinal-group` can’t be verified from the diff alone, but the mixed-syntax compatibility concern is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .small-action flex layout in topic-post.scss removes the 4em avatar clearance so .small-action-desc text touches the avatar edge, and changes spacing of avatar-less small-action blocks

adjudication.rationale: In `topic-post.scss`, `.small-action` is changed to a flex container, and `.small-action-desc` loses its previous `padding-left: 4em` (from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em;`) and now has only `padding: 0 1.5%`. In the diff, `.topic-avatar` has no right margin added, so the removal of the 4em left padding can plausibly eliminate the intended gap between the avatar and the description text, making them sit flush in a flex row. Also, for cases without a `.topic-avatar` element, the left spacing would change from a fixed 4em indent to a small percentage padding, matching the finding’s claim about altered spacing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Flex shrink on header.scss .contents allows a long title/category badge to compress the panel buttons (hamburger, search, user) at narrow desktop widths since no flex-shrink: 0 or min-width is set

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `header.scss` `.contents` from a block with floated children (`.title` float left, `.panel` float right) to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) with `.panel` positioned via `margin-left: auto` and `@include order(3)`. No `flex-shrink: 0`, `min-width`, or `flex` rules are added for `.panel` (or the title area), so under flexbox defaults (`flex: 0 1 auto`) it’s plausible that available space constraints from a long title/badge could cause the panel area to shrink/wrap/overflow compared to the previous float behavior. However, the diff doesn’t show the flex children structure/content (e.g., panel button styles), so the exact “compress the panel buttons” behavior can’t be fully verified from this diff alone.
